originality.rationale: The classical Dirichlet endpoint is a scalar projection (Abdollahi–Mehrangiz 2011); the ordinary Bergman endpoint point spectrum was studied by Abdollahi–Mehrangiz–Roientan 2015 and is explicitly acknowledged as covered. The surviving claim treats all real coefficient-smoothness parameters with an exact critical weak-Schatten defect, equal two-sided logarithmic singular coefficients, and signed degree-filtration anomaly. Checked work on linear-fractional symbols does not imply this. Missing 2015 full text leaves residual historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: The complete 2015 monomial Bergman article was not accessible; its precisely known unweighted scope is excluded from the originality claim, but an undocumented general weighted extension cannot be ruled out.

value.rationale: The canonical Dirichlet-type coefficient scale connects Bergman, Hardy and Dirichlet-type regimes. Essential spectral data collapse the nonnormality defect to a projection and miss the critical compact 1/j correction. The exact two-sided coefficients quantify that missed defect in generalized traces and approximation numbers, while the surprising finite signed degree-filtration limit measures cancellation of two logarithmically divergent absolute tails. These are natural sharp operator-ideal invariants, not arbitrary finite table entries.
